criteria.text: The medication is approved to treat a condition or disease for which no other therapy is approved.
The patient tried and failed at least one other therapy for a condition or disease the new product is approved to treat.
The product qualifies as a reformulation variant under criteria 2(a–f); see notes for the six qualifying categories.
The product qualifies as a reformulation variant under criteria 2(a–f).
The patient tried and failed at least two other therapies for a condition or disease the new product is approved to treat.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid New Prescription Medications: three alternative approval paths with supporting attestations. The one-therapy path is for non-reformulation products; reformulation variants require at least two failed therapies. Documentation and policy applicability require manual review.

Applicability (notes only): new prescription medications, excluding A-rated generic pharmaceutical equivalents, are subject to this PA for at least six (6) months after market launch. After six months the DUR Committee may review whether to remove PA; removal is not automatic.
Preferred-class exception (notes only): if P&T designates the product preferred in a reviewed drug class, this PA is removed and the preferred-class requirements apply instead.

Reformulation variants, criterion 2(a–f): (a) active ingredient available in a different dosage form (capsule, tablet, solution, suspension, emulsion, cream, ointment, gel, etc.); (b) active ingredient available with a different release mechanism (immediate release, extended release, delayed release, depot injection, oral disintegrating tablet, etc.); (c) active ingredient available by a different route (oral, sublingual, buccal, parenteral, rectal, transdermal, etc.); (d) racemic mixture, single enantiomer, diastereomer, or isomer of an available medication; (e) prodrug metabolized to the active ingredient in an available medication; (f) active metabolite of an available medication. is_reformulation_variant attests that at least one of these categories applies.

Criterion 3 (notes only): a new branded product using the same pharmacologic mechanism follows the current prior authorization guidelines for the like drug. No separate machine approval path is encoded.
Length of approval (notes only): up to 12 months. Dispensing limit (notes only): no more than a 30-day supply.
References: Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (Orange Book), http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/ob/default.cfm.
Source: New Product Criteria Version 1; Original 04/16/2010; Last updated 10/8/2020; Approved 11/20/2020. The existing effective_date stub 2022-11-01 is retained; it does not replace the PDF dates.
